question: Is pregame_context_logit a duplicate of the LIVE historical_strength family (f2 = 1), or does it carry information Elo does not?

arm_b_shuffled.note: The same estimator on the same rows with the seven non-strength features permuted in TRAINING, scored on the unpermuted holdout. margin_diff (the strength-class proxy) is never permuted.

duplicate_test.design: permutation test on the repo's own fitBridge/predictBridge. ARM A = real training rows. ARM B = the seven non-strength features permuted in training. margin_diff is never permuted. Bootstrap resamples GAMES, paired, 10,000 replicates.
duplicate_test.verdict: DUPLICATE: the seven non-strength features contribute NOTHING measurable beyond the strength class. Permuting them in training does not degrade the model -- the point estimate is NEGATIVE (permuting them scores BETTER), the 95% CI on their incremental value includes zero, and every one of the 20 permutations beat the full arm. The f2 = 1 duplicate claim HOLDS on the measurement. The burden is on showing the extra information exists, and it does not.
duplicate_test.verdict_logic: One-sided. To REFUTE the duplicate claim, permuting the seven features must DEGRADE the model in >95% of paired bootstrap replicates. It degrades in only 26.6%. The duplicate claim is therefore confirmed, and the burden of proof for the extra information lies with the claimant.
duplicate_test.permutations_beating_full_arm_note: 20 of 20 permutations scored BELOW the full arm. Permuting the seven non-strength features in training made the model slightly BETTER on the holdout, which is what overfitting noise features looks like.

calibration.note: The repo's C-290 concern (docs/engine/research/2026-10-02/corpus-deep/deep/c03/challenges.md item 20) was that the raw binned ECE is upward-biased at n=285 and the 'eligible' call is too conservative. MEASURED: the debiased estimator does read lower, but BOTH pass the 0.06 gate, so the ECE gate is not the blocker.

reproduction_check.note: The published holdout doc reports skill +0.026190 against the TRAINING base rate (0.564297, 6,991 rows of 1999-2024). This script reports +0.025146 against the 2025 HOLDOUT's own base rate (0.533333). Both are correct; the base rate differs by construction. The Brier (0.223743) and the raw ECE (0.051868) reproduce EXACTLY, which is the check that matters: the estimator, the features and the split are the published ones.
